It was raining hard, and the power had gone. No TV, no fan. Yogesh lay on the floor.
"Arnab Mama, I'm bored. Give me your phone."
"The battery is low. We need it."
"But I'm BORED."
Arnab Mama did not argue. He put three steel bowls, two spoons and an old newspaper on the floor, and went back to his tea.
Yogesh sulked. Then he tapped a bowl with a spoon. Ting. A bigger bowl. Dong. He rolled the newspaper into a trumpet.
Ten minutes later he was marching round the room, a one-boy band, louder than the rain.

qa.a: He put three steel bowls, two spoons and an old newspaper on the floor.

qa.q: How was Yogesh feeling before he tapped the bowl?
qa.a: He felt bored and grumpy, and he sulked when he couldn't have the phone.

qa.a: He did not argue or give the phone; he left simple things and gave time, so Yogesh's boredom led him to invent a band.

qa.q: What would change if Arnab Mama had handed over the phone?
qa.a: Yogesh might have stopped feeling bored for a while, but he would not have discovered the bowls and made his own band.

grounding: It shows a young child who is bored during a power cut asking for a phone, and finding a game when an adult gives time and simple things.
